question: Is section 160 of the Penal Code, on supplying drugs or instruments to procure an abortion, still good law?
notes: Status: in force; its validity has been tested in court. HC in PAK & another v AG [2022] KEHC 262 upheld s.160 (no limit recorded).

question: Has any court struck down section 379A of the Criminal Procedure Code?
notes: Status: in force; validity tested. CORD v Republic [2015] KEHC 7074 upheld s.379A; it was not struck down.

question: Can I still rely on s.78A of the Evidence Act to admit electronic evidence, or has it been challenged?
notes: Status: in force; validity tested. CORD v Republic [2015] KEHC 7074 upheld s.78A.

question: What is the current status of section 333 of the CPC?
notes: Status: in force; interpreted by a court. Pamba v Republic [2025] KECA 793 (ruling) interpreted s.333 (warrant / sentence computation).

question: Is section 49 of the Criminal Procedure Code still in force?
notes: Status: declared unconstitutional. Mbuti & 5 others v AG [2015] KEHC 6970 declared s.49 (part of the security-for-good-behaviour scheme) unconstitutional.

question: Is the death penalty for treason still mandatory in Kenya after the Supreme Court's death-sentence rulings?
notes: Penal Code s.40 (treason). Status: in force; interpreted by a court. Muruatetu 2021 directions [2021] KESC 31 said the 2017 decision applies only to murder under ss.203/204, so it does not extend to treason.

question: In a criminal trial, can the prosecution and the defence agree in writing on facts that aren't in dispute, and has that procedure survived a constitutional challenge?
notes: Evidence Act s.59A. Status: in force; validity tested. Upheld in CORD v Republic [2015] KEHC 7074.

question: Is it still an offence in Kenya to engage in so-called subversive activities against the government?
notes: Penal Code s.77. Status: declared unconstitutional by Katiba Institute & 8 others v DPP [2024] KEHC 2890.

question: Does the law still let the prosecution withhold the identity of witnesses or limit disclosure to the accused under the 2014 security law amendments?
notes: CPC s.42A (disclosure by prosecution). Status: declared unconstitutional in CORD v Republic [2015] KEHC 7074.

question: Can someone be prosecuted for posting obscene content online under Kenya's communications law?
notes: KICA s.84D. Status: declared unconstitutional in Cyprian Andama v DPP [2019] KEHC 4927.

question: What did the court decide in Mbuti?
notes: Mbuti & 5 others v AG [2015] KEHC 6970: declared CPC ss.43-61A (security for keeping the peace / good behaviour) unconstitutional; ss.43, 44, 45 at least should be named. All in effect.

question: What happened in Kahinga?
notes: Joseph Kaberia Kahinga & 11 others v AG [2016] KEHC 3275: partial declarations of unconstitutionality on Penal Code ss.295 and 296 (robbery). s.295 limited by a court; s.296 limited by a court (in effect).

question: Tell me about Kittiny.
notes: William Okungu Kittiny v Republic [2018] KECA 851: CA declared the mandatory death sentence in s.296 unconstitutional (partial); that ruling is displaced by a later ruling. s.296 status: limited by a court.

question: What did the High Court hold in Wachira & 12 others v Republic & 2 others (2022) about minimum sentences in the Sexual Offences Act?
notes: Wachira [2022] KEHC 12795: partial declarations on SOA ss.3, 8, 11, 20 (mandatory minimums). On ss.3, 11, 20 in effect; on s.8 (979) displaced by later SC rulings (Mwangi [2024] KESC 34).

question: What was the outcome of Kenya Union of Journalists v Communications Authority of Kenya?
notes: KUJ v CA [2024] KEHC 13677: KICA ss.46A and 46H declared unconstitutional in part. Both: limited by a court.

question: In Jirongo v Soy Developers Ltd, what did the Supreme Court say about running criminal and civil cases at the same time?
notes: Jirongo v Soy Developers [2021] KESC 32 interpreted CPC s.193A (concurrent criminal and civil proceedings). Status: in force; interpreted by a court.

question: How have the courts treated the mandatory death sentence for robbery with violence over the years?
notes: Penal Code s.296. Status: limited by a court. In effect: Kahinga [2016] KEHC 3275 (964), Muruatetu 2021 directions (1019), Manya [2025] KECA 2293 (916, upheld). Displaced: Mwaura 2013 (1028), Koibata (927), Kittiny 2018 (883), Ramadhan 2024 (996), Imutoka 2024 (910), Kamau 2024 (1071).

question: Are the minimum sentences for defilement still mandatory, given the Court of Appeal decisions that let judges go below them?
notes: SOA s.8. Status: in force; earlier court limits were reversed. Mwangi [2022] KECA 1106 (E11) reversed on appeal by SC [2024] KESC 34 (E13); Kilwake [2019] KECA 5 (E09) and HC read-downs/declarations (Wambogo, Maingi, Wachira, Rono) displaced by a later ruling.

question: Was the life sentence for defiling a child under eleven ever found unconstitutional, and where does it stand now?
notes: SOA s.8. Status: in force; earlier court limits were reversed. Manyeso [2023] KECA 827 (E12) reversed by Republic v Manyeso [2025] KESC 16 (E14); Ayako [2023] KECA 1563 (E18) reversed by [2025] KESC 20 (E15). E13 (SC Mwangi 2024) also relevant.

question: Is section 299 of the Criminal Procedure Code still part of the law?
notes: CPC s.299 repealed by statute; no court rulings on record. Answer should say repealed and cite no rulings.

question: My notes cite section 164 of the Penal Code. Is it still in force?
notes: Penal Code s.164 repealed by statute; no court rulings on record.

question: Has any court limited Article 159 of the Constitution on judicial authority?
notes: Art. 159: no court rulings on record in Hakiki; in force. Answer should say Hakiki holds no ruling on it, not invent one.

question: Are there any decisions recorded against the equality and non-discrimination article of the Constitution?
notes: Art. 27: no court rulings on record in Hakiki; in force. Must not invent rulings.

question: Has any court struck down section 49 of the Traffic Act?
notes: Traffic Act (Cap. 403) is not held by Hakiki; answer should say so and not guess.

question: What is the current status of the Children Act 2022 provisions on parental responsibility?
notes: Children Act 2022 is not held by Hakiki; answer should say so.

question: What was decided in Mukisa Biscuit Manufacturing Co v West End Distributors about preliminary objections?
notes: Not held (controller checked: no title match). Answer says it is not in Hakiki's collection and invents no holding. Replaced Mitu-Bell, which Hakiki holds.

question: What test for an interlocutory injunction did the court set in Giella v Cassman Brown?
notes: Not held (controller checked: no title match). Answer says it is not in Hakiki's collection and invents no holding. Replaced BAT v Ministry of Health, which Hakiki holds.

question: Police arrested me at night without a warrant for a petty offence. Was that lawful and what should I do?
notes: CPC s.21 (arrest). Status: limited by a court: read down in Katiba Institute v AG [2022] KEHC 17072. No legal advice; report what the sources say and suggest an advocate.

question: I got the maximum sentence for stealing a phone. Can I appeal the sentence as too harsh?
notes: Penal Code s.275. Status: in force; interpreted by a court in Kwaka v Republic [2022] KEHC 16963. No legal advice; refer to an advocate.

question: I'm charged with rape but no DNA or medical test was done. Can my lawyer argue the case must fail without it?
notes: SOA s.36. Status: in force; interpreted by a court in Lumbasi v Republic [2016] KEHC 2942 (medical/forensic evidence not mandatory). No legal advice; refer to an advocate.
